reviewer.title: SA2 Reviewer
reviewer.description: Comprehensive SA2 reviewer grounded exclusively in Module 3: Software Development and Design and Module 4: Understanding and Using APIs. Fill-in-the-blank questions are excluded.

questions.question: Which description best defines the software development life cycle (SDLC)?
questions.explanation: SDLC is the process of developing software from an idea through delivery.
choices: A process limited to coding and debugging
A process of developing software from an idea through delivery
A process used only after software reaches production
A process for managing only source-code repositories
questions.correctAnswer: A process of developing software from an idea through delivery

questions.question: Which four activities are explicitly included in SDLC beyond just coding? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The module states that SDLC includes gathering requirements, creating a proof of concept, testing, and fixing bugs.

questions.question: At the conclusion of the requirements and analysis phase, what document does the classic waterfall method suggest creating?
questions.explanation: The classic waterfall method suggests creating a Software Requirement Specification (SRS) that states requirements and scope.

questions.question: After requirements are gathered, which four questions does the team analyze? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The requirements and analysis phase evaluates feasibility and budget, schedule risks, testing, and delivery.
choices: Whether development is possible and can be done on-budget
Whether there are risks to the development schedule
How the software will be tested
When and how the software will be delivered
Which Git transport protocol must be used
Which webhook provider must be registered
correctAnswers: Whether development is possible and can be done on-budget
Whether there are risks to the development schedule
How the software will be tested
When and how the software will be delivered

questions.question: Which documents are created at the end of the Design phase?
questions.explanation: The Design phase produces High-Level Design and Low-Level Design documents.

questions.question: Why is the implementation phase described as the longest phase of the life cycle?
questions.explanation: All components and modules are built during implementation.
choices: All components and modules are built during it
All customer support requests are handled during it
Every stakeholder requirement is first gathered during it
The production environment is created during it
questions.correctAnswer: All components and modules are built during it

questions.question: Which four types of testing are explicitly performed during the Testing phase? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The module lists functional, integration, performance, and security testing.

questions.question: Which four activities occur during the Maintenance phase? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: Maintenance includes customer support, production bug fixes, software improvements, and gathering new customer requests.
choices: Gather new requests from the customer
Install code in the test environment
correctAnswers: Gather new requests from the customer

questions.question: Which three methodologies are identified as the most popular software development methodologies?
questions.explanation: The module identifies Waterfall, Agile, and Lean.

questions.question: Which three factors does the module say influence the choice of software development methodology? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: The choice depends on project type, project length, and team size.

questions.question: Who created the original waterfall model described in the module?
questions.explanation: The original waterfall model was created by Winston W. Royce.

questions.question: Which four statements are values of the Agile Manifesto? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The Agile Manifesto values individuals and interactions, working software, customer collaboration, and responding to change over their paired alternatives.
choices: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Responding to change over following a plan
Following a plan over responding to change
correctAnswers: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Responding to change over following a plan

questions.question: Which Agile method focuses on small, self-organizing teams that meet daily for short periods and work in iterative sprints?
questions.explanation: The module describes Agile Scrum this way.

questions.question: Which Agile method prescribes development in terms of an overall model that is broken out, planned, designed, and built feature-by-feature?
questions.explanation: This is the module's description of Feature-Driven Development (FDD).

questions.question: A team fixes a 3-week period and selects user stories it believes it can finish during that period. What is this period called?
questions.explanation: A sprint is a specific period, usually 2–4 weeks, in which a team takes on tasks or user stories it can accomplish.

questions.question: What is the backlog in Agile development?
questions.explanation: The backlog is a prioritized list containing all features of the software.
choices: A prioritized list of all software features
A list of only completed user stories
A record of Git merge conflicts
questions.correctAnswer: A prioritized list of all software features

questions.question: Which statement best describes a user story?
questions.explanation: A user story is a simple statement of what a user or role needs and why, and it should be small enough for one team to finish in one sprint.
choices: A detailed record of every source-code change
A simple statement of what a user or role needs and why
A list of all defects found in production
A document describing only software architecture
questions.correctAnswer: A simple statement of what a user or role needs and why

questions.question: A Scrum team should be larger than 10 individuals to remain cross-functional.
questions.explanation: The module states that Scrum teams should not be larger than 10 individuals.

questions.question: What is the stated maximum duration of a daily Scrum stand-up meeting?
questions.explanation: The Scrum master should hold the daily stand-up for not more than 15 minutes.

questions.question: What is the fundamental focus of Lean software development?
questions.explanation: Lean is based on principles focused on minimizing waste and maximizing value to the customer.
choices: Minimizing waste and maximizing customer value
Maximizing team size and minimizing iterations
Eliminating testing and maximizing deployment speed
questions.correctAnswer: Minimizing waste and maximizing customer value

questions.question: Which seven items are identified as wastes of software development? Select 7 answers.
questions.explanation: The module lists partially done work, extra processes, extra features, task switching, waiting, motion, and defects.

questions.question: According to the module, which three outcomes are enabled by frequent short iterations of working software? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: Short iterations help developers learn faster, let customers give feedback sooner, and allow features to be adjusted for more customer value.
choices: Features can be adjusted to bring customers more value
All decisions must be made earlier
correctAnswers: Features can be adjusted to bring customers more value

questions.question: Why does Lean recommend deciding as late as possible when uncertainty exists?
questions.explanation: The module says decisions should be based on facts rather than opinions or speculation.
choices: To base decisions on facts rather than opinions or speculation
To prevent developers from making decisions
questions.correctAnswer: To base decisions on facts rather than opinions or speculation

questions.question: The Lean principle 'Empower the Team' allows each person to make decisions in the area of their own expertise.
questions.explanation: This is the module's description of empowering the team.

questions.question: What does 'Optimize the Whole' emphasize?
questions.explanation: Software should be built cohesively; experts should consider the effects of their decisions on the rest of the software.
choices: Each expert should focus only on their own area
Software should be built cohesively with attention to effects across the whole
Every decision should be delayed indefinitely
Only customer-facing components should be optimized
questions.correctAnswer: Software should be built cohesively with attention to effects across the whole

questions.question: What are software design patterns?
questions.explanation: They are best-practice solutions for common software development problems.
choices: Best-practice solutions for common software development problems
Testing scripts that replace design documents
questions.correctAnswer: Best-practice solutions for common software development problems

questions.question: Software design patterns are language-independent.
questions.explanation: The module explicitly states that design patterns are language-independent.

questions.question: Which three main categories did the Gang of Four use for design patterns? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: The three categories are creational, structural, and behavioral.

questions.question: Which commonly used design pattern is identified as a Behavioral design pattern?
questions.explanation: The Observer design pattern is identified as Behavioral.

questions.question: Which two capabilities must the subject provide to implement the Observer subscription mechanism? Select 2 answers.
questions.explanation: The subject stores a list of observers and provides methods to add and remove observers.
choices: Store a list of all observers
Provide methods to add and remove observers
Create a new repository for each observer
correctAnswers: Store a list of all observers
Provide methods to add and remove observers

questions.question: What benefit of the Observer pattern is emphasized in the module?
questions.explanation: Observers can receive real-time data from the subject when a change occurs.
choices: Observers can receive real-time data when the subject changes
Observers eliminate the need for subjects
Observers convert local repositories into remote repositories
Observers guarantee that code contains no bugs
questions.correctAnswer: Observers can receive real-time data when the subject changes

questions.question: In MVC, which component manages the application's data, logic, and rules?
questions.explanation: The Model is the application's data structure and manages its data, logic, and rules.

questions.question: In MVC, which component acts as the middleman between the model and view?
questions.explanation: The Controller takes user input and manipulates it into a format for the model or view.

questions.question: What development benefit of MVC is stated in the module?
questions.explanation: Each MVC component can be built in parallel.
choices: Each component can be built in parallel
It removes the need for user input
It stores all application data in the view
questions.correctAnswer: Each component can be built in parallel

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of version control?
questions.explanation: Version control manages changes to files and keeps a history of those changes.
choices: Manage changes to files and keep their history
questions.correctAnswer: Manage changes to files and keep their history

questions.question: Which five benefits of version control are listed? Select 5 answers.
questions.explanation: The module lists collaboration, accountability and visibility, work in isolation, safety, and work anywhere.

questions.question: Which three types of version control systems are identified? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: The module identifies local, centralized, and distributed systems.

questions.question: What does an LVCS usually store between two versions of a file?
questions.explanation: In most cases, an LVCS stores the delta between file versions.
choices: The delta between the two versions
questions.correctAnswer: The delta between the two versions

questions.question: Which model does a centralized version control system use?
questions.explanation: CVCS uses a server-client model with a centralized repository.

questions.question: Why does a CVCS require a user to check out a file before modifying it?
questions.explanation: The module states that only one individual can work on a particular file at a time, so the file is checked out to lock it.
choices: To lock the file while that individual works on it
To convert the file into a snapshot
To add the file to a webhook
questions.correctAnswer: To lock the file while that individual works on it

questions.question: Why is file locking not required in a DVCS?
questions.explanation: Each individual modifies a local file in a working copy, so multiple individuals can work on a file at the same time.
choices: Only one user is permitted in the repository
Each user modifies a local working copy
DVCS does not keep file history
DVCS prevents users from editing the same file
questions.correctAnswer: Each user modifies a local working copy

questions.question: How does Git primarily store versioned data?
questions.explanation: Git stores data as snapshots rather than differences between current and previous files.

questions.question: If a file has not changed, Git can use a reference link to the last snapshot instead of taking an identical new snapshot.
questions.explanation: The module explicitly describes this behavior.

questions.question: Which three stages are part of Git's 'organized by 3s' model? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: Git's three stages are repository, working directory, and staging area.

questions.question: Which three states are part of Git's 'organized by 3s' model? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: The three states are committed, modified, and staged.

questions.question: Where is a local Git repository stored?
questions.explanation: A local repository is stored on the file system of the client machine where Git commands are executed.
choices: On the client machine's file system
Only on a repository hosting service
Inside the remote server's working directory
questions.correctAnswer: On the client machine's file system

questions.question: After cloning, a local and remote Git repository remain automatically synchronized without manual Git commands.
questions.explanation: The module states that the repositories are independent until changes are applied through manual Git command execution.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of branching in Git?
questions.explanation: Branching lets users work independently without affecting the main code in the repository.
choices: Work on code independently without affecting the main code
Force all users to edit the same working copy
questions.correctAnswer: Work on code independently without affecting the main code

questions.question: When switching Git branches, the repository (.git) directory changes to match the selected branch.
questions.explanation: The working directory and staging area change, but the .git repository directory remains unchanged.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes Git from GitHub according to the module?
questions.explanation: Git is a distributed version control implementation; GitHub is a repository hosting service that uses Git.
choices: Git is a DVCS implementation, while GitHub is a repository hosting service using Git
GitHub is a local version control system, while Git is a code review method
Git and GitHub are two names for the same software
Git is a hosting service, while GitHub is a command-line DVCS implementation
questions.correctAnswer: Git is a DVCS implementation, while GitHub is a repository hosting service using Git

questions.question: What is a GitHub pull request?
questions.explanation: It formalizes a contributor's request to review branch changes for inclusion in a main or curated branch.
choices: A request to review branch changes for possible inclusion in another branch
A command that deletes a local repository
A method for creating an SRS
A request that automatically resolves all merge conflicts
questions.correctAnswer: A request to review branch changes for possible inclusion in another branch

questions.question: Which command creates an empty Git repository or makes an existing folder a Git repository?
questions.explanation: The git init command initializes a Git repository.

questions.question: What hidden directory is created when a project becomes a Git repository?
questions.explanation: Git creates a hidden .git directory containing repository metadata.

questions.question: Which four transport protocols does Git support for accessing a repository as listed in the module? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The listed protocols are Local, SSH, Git, and HTTP.

questions.question: Which Git command lists files that differ between the working directory and the parent branch?
questions.explanation: git status provides this list.

questions.question: Which Git command is described as a generic file comparison tool?
questions.explanation: git diff is the generic file comparison tool.

questions.question: Which command stages all changed files?
questions.explanation: The module gives git add . for adding all changed files to the staging area.

questions.question: What does `git rm --cached <file>` do?
questions.explanation: It stages the file's removal from the Git repository without removing the file itself from the working directory.
choices: Stages removal from Git while preserving the file in the working directory
Deletes the file from both Git and the working directory without staging
Restores the file from the remote repository
Moves the file directly into the repository
questions.correctAnswer: Stages removal from Git while preserving the file in the working directory

questions.question: What does `git commit` do with changes in the staging area?
questions.explanation: It combines staged content changes into a single commit and updates the local repository.
choices: Combines staged changes into a single commit and updates the local repository
Uploads working-directory changes directly to a remote repository
questions.correctAnswer: Combines staged changes into a single commit and updates the local repository

questions.question: Which command updates the master branch of the remote repository from the local repository?
questions.explanation: The module gives `git push origin master` for this operation.

questions.question: Which command updates a local copy of a Git repository from the remote repository?
questions.explanation: git pull manually updates the local repository and working content.

questions.question: Which command deletes a Git branch?
questions.explanation: The module specifies `git branch -d <branch name>`.

questions.question: During a Git merge, which branch is modified?
questions.explanation: Only the target branch is modified; the source branch remains unchanged.

questions.question: What is a fast-forward merge as defined in the module?
questions.explanation: It occurs when Git can apply source changes to the target automatically without conflicts.
choices: A merge Git can apply automatically without conflicts
A merge that always deletes the source branch
A merge that requires manual conflict resolution
A merge that updates only a remote repository
questions.correctAnswer: A merge Git can apply automatically without conflicts

questions.question: When does a merge conflict occur?
questions.explanation: A merge conflict occurs when Git does not know how to automatically apply branch changes together for the files.
choices: When Git cannot automatically combine branch changes for the files
Whenever a new branch is created
When a repository has no remote
questions.correctAnswer: When Git cannot automatically combine branch changes for the files

questions.question: Which command joins two or more Git branches together?
questions.explanation: Git provides the git merge command to join branches.

questions.question: In a unified .diff file, which three symbol-to-meaning mappings are correct? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: A plus indicates an added line, a minus indicates a removed line, and @@ indicates the next information block.
choices: @@ indicates the next block of information
index means a line was removed
correctAnswers: @@ indicates the next block of information

questions.question: What is the main goal of clean code described in the module?
questions.explanation: Clean code is written to be easy for other developers to read and understand.
choices: Make code easy for other developers to read and understand
Make code depend on one large function
questions.correctAnswer: Make code easy for other developers to read and understand

questions.question: Which four characteristics are emphasized by clean code? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The module emphasizes standardization, proper organization, modularity, and inline comments among characteristics that make code self-documenting.

questions.question: Which code is especially likely to be a candidate for encapsulation in a method or function?
questions.explanation: Task code used more than once should probably be encapsulated.
choices: Task code used more than once
Only code that can never be reused
questions.correctAnswer: Task code used more than once

questions.question: Methods and functions can be written once and executed as many times as required.
questions.explanation: The module explicitly states this as a benefit of methods and functions.

questions.question: What do arguments and parameters add to methods and functions?
questions.explanation: They add flexibility.

questions.question: What happens when a Python return statement is executed?
questions.explanation: It returns the specified value, ends the function's execution, and skips code below it.
choices: The function ends and code below the return is skipped
The function restarts from its first line
The code below it always executes before returning
questions.correctAnswer: The function ends and code below the return is skipped

questions.question: How does the module distinguish a method from a function?
questions.explanation: Methods are associated with an object, while functions are standalone code blocks.
choices: Methods are associated with an object; functions are standalone
Functions are associated with an object; methods are standalone
Methods can never be reused; functions can
questions.correctAnswer: Methods are associated with an object; functions are standalone

questions.question: Why do developers typically use modules?
questions.explanation: Modules divide large projects into smaller parts that are easier to read and understand.
choices: To divide large projects into smaller, understandable parts
To eliminate all interfaces between code components
To force all code into a single file
To replace classes with Git branches
questions.correctAnswer: To divide large projects into smaller, understandable parts

questions.question: How is a module packaged according to the module?
questions.explanation: A module is packaged as a single file and is expected to work independently.
choices: As a single file expected to work independently
As a required set of remote repositories
As multiple files that cannot work independently
questions.correctAnswer: As a single file expected to work independently

questions.question: What does each class declaration define?
questions.explanation: Each class declaration defines a new object type.

questions.question: In Python, a single preceding underscore is conventionally used to indicate methods or variables considered private.
questions.explanation: The module notes this convention even though Python does not provide private class variables or internal methods in the same way described for other OOP languages.

questions.question: When does the code review process occur according to the module?
questions.explanation: Code review happens after code changes are complete and tested.
choices: After code changes are complete and tested
Only after deployment to end users
questions.correctAnswer: After code changes are complete and tested

questions.question: Which four code review types are listed? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The module lists formal, change-based, over-the-shoulder, and email pass-around reviews.

questions.question: Which type of code review uses a series of meetings to review the whole codebase?
questions.explanation: This is a formal code review.

questions.question: Which type of code review examines code changed because of a bug, user story, feature, or commit?
questions.explanation: This is change-based, or tool-assisted, code review.

questions.question: Which testing category asks whether software behaves correctly in a logical sense?
questions.explanation: Functional testing determines whether the software works correctly.

questions.question: Which four concerns are examples of non-functional testing listed in the module? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: Non-functional testing includes usability, performance, security, resiliency, compliance, localization, and other issues.

questions.question: What is unit testing?
questions.explanation: Unit testing is detailed functional testing of small pieces of code in isolation.
choices: Detailed functional testing of small pieces of code in isolation
Testing only the complete application after deployment
Reviewing the entire codebase in meetings
questions.correctAnswer: Detailed functional testing of small pieces of code in isolation

questions.question: Which Python testing framework automatically executes appropriately named test scripts and functions as described in the module?
questions.explanation: PyTest automatically executes scripts and functions that follow the stated test naming conventions.

questions.question: What does Python's unittest framework require according to the module?
questions.explanation: For unittest, the tester subclasses the built-in TestCase class and uses or adds methods whose names begin with test_.
choices: Subclass TestCase and use test_ methods
Store tests only in the staging area
Use only functions ending in _test.py without a class
questions.correctAnswer: Subclass TestCase and use test_ methods

questions.question: What is the purpose of integration testing?
questions.explanation: Integration testing ensures individual units fit together properly to form a complete application.
choices: Ensure individual units fit together into a complete application
Test each isolated line without considering other units
questions.correctAnswer: Ensure individual units fit together into a complete application

questions.question: In Test-Driven Development, what is written before the application code?
questions.explanation: Testing code is written first to express requirements, then application code is written until it passes the tests.

questions.question: Which five steps form the repeating TDD process? Select 5 answers.
questions.explanation: The module lists creating a test, running tests, writing application code to pass it, running tests again, and refactoring/improving the code.
choices: Run tests to see if any fail for unexpected reasons
Write application code to pass the new test
Run tests to see if any fail
correctAnswers: Run tests to see if any fail for unexpected reasons
Write application code to pass the new test
Run tests to see if any fail

questions.question: Which three formats are identified as the most popular standard formats for exchanging information with remote APIs? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: The module identifies XML, JSON, and YAML.

questions.question: What is XML?
questions.explanation: XML is a generic methodology for wrapping textual data in symmetrical tags to indicate semantics.
choices: A methodology for wrapping textual data in symmetrical tags to indicate semantics
questions.correctAnswer: A methodology for wrapping textual data in symmetrical tags to indicate semantics

questions.question: Which four basic data types does JSON include? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The module lists numbers, strings, Booleans, and nulls.

questions.question: JSON supports a standard method for including unparsed comments in code.
questions.explanation: The module states that JSON does not support a standard method for comments.

questions.question: Whitespace in JSON is significant to the meaning of the document.
questions.explanation: The module states that whitespace in JSON is not significant.

questions.question: How is YAML related to JSON according to the module?
questions.explanation: YAML is described as a superset of JSON designed for easier human readability.
choices: YAML is a superset of JSON designed for easier human readability
JSON is a superset of YAML
YAML and JSON cannot represent similar data
YAML is a version control format
questions.correctAnswer: YAML is a superset of JSON designed for easier human readability

questions.question: YAML parsers can generally parse JSON documents, but JSON parsers cannot generally parse YAML documents.
questions.explanation: This follows from the module's description of YAML as a superset of JSON.

questions.question: How does YAML indicate hierarchy?
questions.explanation: YAML indicates hierarchy using indentation.

questions.question: Which conventional markers open and close a YAML file as described in the module?
questions.explanation: YAML files conventionally open with three dashes and end with three dots.

questions.question: How are YAML comments introduced?
questions.explanation: Comments are preceded by a hash sign and a space, except where excluded by the long-string rule described in the module.
choices: With a hash sign and a space
questions.correctAnswer: With a hash sign and a space

questions.question: What does parsing mean?
questions.explanation: Parsing analyzes a message, breaks it into component parts, and understands their purposes in context.
choices: Analyzing a message and breaking it into meaningful component parts
Turning every message into a Git snapshot
Uploading a local repository to a remote
questions.correctAnswer: Analyzing a message and breaking it into meaningful component parts

questions.question: What does serialization do in relation to parsing?
questions.explanation: Serialization is roughly the opposite: it turns internal data structures into semantically equivalent messages formatted as character strings.
choices: Turns internal data structures into semantically equivalent character-string messages
Breaks incoming messages into typed internal structures
Creates a Git branch for each data object
Converts all API calls to webhooks
questions.correctAnswer: Turns internal data structures into semantically equivalent character-string messages

questions.question: What does an Application Programming Interface (API) allow?
questions.explanation: An API allows one piece of software to talk to another.
choices: One piece of software to talk to another
A Git branch to merge itself automatically
A server to eliminate all authentication
A user story to become a sprint
questions.correctAnswer: One piece of software to talk to another

questions.question: What does an API determine about an application?
questions.explanation: It determines what data, services, and functionality the application exposes to third parties.
choices: What data, services, and functionality are exposed to third parties
Which code review type must be used
How many Scrum members are allowed
questions.correctAnswer: What data, services, and functionality are exposed to third parties

questions.question: Which three API use cases are listed in the module? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: The listed use cases are automation tasks, data integration, and functionality integration.

questions.question: APIs are built only for human interaction and cannot be consumed programmatically by applications.
questions.explanation: APIs are built to be consumed programmatically, although humans may also interact with them manually.

questions.question: Which development change helped non-software engineers build applications and consume APIs?
questions.explanation: The module cites simplified coding languages such as Python.
choices: Simplified coding languages such as Python
Replacement of APIs with local files
questions.correctAnswer: Simplified coding languages such as Python

questions.question: How does a synchronous API respond to a request?
questions.explanation: It responds directly by providing data immediately.
choices: It always sends a response with no data
It requires the client to register a webhook first
It delays every response until another request arrives

questions.question: When is a synchronous API appropriate according to the module?
questions.explanation: APIs are synchronous when requested data is readily available.
choices: When the requested data is readily available
Only when the server requires hours to process the request
questions.correctAnswer: When the requested data is readily available

questions.question: With a synchronous API, the requesting application must wait for the response before performing additional code execution tasks.
questions.explanation: The module explicitly states this client-side behavior.

questions.question: What initial response does an asynchronous API provide?
questions.explanation: It provides a response with no data to signify that the request has been received.
choices: A response with no data acknowledging receipt
The completed data in every case
A SOAP Fault in every case
questions.correctAnswer: A response with no data acknowledging receipt

questions.question: When is an API asynchronous according to the module?
questions.explanation: It is asynchronous when processing takes time or the data is not readily available.
choices: When processing takes time or data is not readily available
Only when data is immediately available
questions.correctAnswer: When processing takes time or data is not readily available

questions.question: What is a benefit of asynchronous API design?
questions.explanation: The application can continue executing without being blocked while the server processes the request.
choices: The application can continue execution without waiting for server processing
The server always returns completed data immediately
The client never needs to handle a response
questions.correctAnswer: The application can continue execution without waiting for server processing

questions.question: Which three API architectural styles are identified as the most popular? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: The module identifies RPC, SOAP, and REST.

questions.question: What is Remote Procedure Call (RPC)?
questions.explanation: RPC is a request-response model that lets an application make a procedure call to another application.
choices: A request-response model for calling a procedure in another application
questions.correctAnswer: A request-response model for calling a procedure in another application

questions.question: Which four transport protocols or forms are listed as examples to which the RPC style can be applied? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The module lists XML-RPC, JSON-RPC, NFS, and SOAP.

questions.question: What type of messaging protocol is SOAP?
questions.explanation: SOAP is an XML-based messaging protocol.

questions.question: Which three characteristics of SOAP are listed? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: SOAP is described as independent, extensible, and neutral.

questions.question: Which four elements may appear in a SOAP message? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: A SOAP XML document may contain Envelope, Header, Body, and Fault.

questions.question: Which SOAP element is the root element of the XML document?
questions.explanation: The Envelope is the root element.

questions.question: Which SOAP element provides error and/or status information?
questions.explanation: The Fault element provides error or status information.

questions.question: Who authored the REST architectural style identified in the module?
questions.explanation: REST is described as authored by Roy Thomas Fielding.

questions.question: What does the REST client-server constraint require?
questions.explanation: Client and server should be independent of each other.
choices: The client and server should be independent
The server must store every client session state
The client and server must run on the same platform
The client must contain the server's data model
questions.correctAnswer: The client and server should be independent

questions.question: What does REST's stateless constraint require of client requests?
questions.explanation: Requests must contain all information the server needs, and the server cannot contain session states.
choices: Requests contain all information needed by the server
The server stores session state for every client
Requests omit information already used previously
questions.correctAnswer: Requests contain all information needed by the server

questions.question: Under the REST cache constraint, what must server responses state?
questions.explanation: Responses must state whether they are cacheable or non-cacheable.
choices: Whether the response is cacheable or non-cacheable
Whether the server has a staging area
questions.correctAnswer: Whether the response is cacheable or non-cacheable

questions.question: Which four principles are listed under REST's uniform interface constraint? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The module lists identification of resources, manipulation through representations, self-descriptive messages, and hypermedia as the engine of application state.
choices: Hypermedia as the engine of application state
correctAnswers: Hypermedia as the engine of application state

questions.question: In REST's layered system, what relationship exists between adjacent layers?
questions.explanation: Each layer provides services only to the layer above and consumes services from the layer below.
choices: Each layer serves the layer above and consumes services from the layer below
Every layer communicates only with the client
Layers cannot consume services from other layers
Every layer must expose the same functions
questions.correctAnswer: Each layer serves the layer above and consumes services from the layer below

questions.question: Code-on-demand is an optional REST constraint because executing third-party code can introduce security risks.
questions.explanation: The module explicitly gives this reason for making code-on-demand optional.

questions.question: Over which protocol does a REST Web service API communicate?
questions.explanation: A REST API communicates over HTTP.

questions.question: Which four major components make up a REST API request? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The request components are URI, HTTP Method, Header, and Body.

questions.question: Which URI component specifies whether HTTP or HTTPS should be used?
questions.explanation: The scheme specifies the HTTP protocol.

questions.question: Which two parts make up the authority component of a URI?
questions.explanation: Authority consists of host and port.

questions.question: Which URI component represents the location of the resource to be manipulated on the server?
questions.explanation: The path identifies the resource location.

questions.question: Which URI component provides details for scope, filtering, or clarification of a request?
questions.explanation: The query component provides those additional details.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is suggested for creating a new object or resource?
questions.explanation: POST maps to Create.

questions.question: Which HTTP method retrieves resource details from the system?
questions.explanation: GET maps to Read.

questions.question: Which HTTP method replaces or updates an existing resource?
questions.explanation: PUT maps to Update.

questions.question: Which HTTP method updates only some details of an existing resource?
questions.explanation: PATCH maps to Partial Update.

questions.question: Which HTTP method removes a resource from the system?
questions.explanation: DELETE maps to Delete.

questions.question: How are HTTP headers formatted?
questions.explanation: Headers are name-value pairs separated by a colon.
choices: As name-value pairs separated by a colon
As values separated only by spaces
questions.correctAnswer: As name-value pairs separated by a colon

questions.question: Which header key can provide credentials to authorize a request?
questions.explanation: The module gives Authorization as the request-header key.

questions.question: Which header key specifies the format of data in the request body?
questions.explanation: Content-Type is the entity header used to specify the body's data format.

questions.question: Which three HTTP methods typically include a request body? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: The module states that POST, PUT, and PATCH typically include a body.

questions.question: Which three major components make up a REST API response? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: REST API responses contain HTTP Status, Header, and Body.

questions.question: What does the first digit of a three-digit HTTP status code indicate?
questions.explanation: The first digit indicates the response category.

questions.question: Which five HTTP status-code category mappings are correct? Select 5 answers.
questions.explanation: The module maps 1xx to Informational, 2xx to Success, 3xx to Redirection, 4xx to Client Error, and 5xx to Server Error.

questions.question: Which status code indicates that a requested resource was created?
questions.explanation: 201 Created means the request was fulfilled and the requested resource was created.

questions.question: Which status code means a request was accepted for processing and is still in process?
questions.explanation: 202 Accepted has this meaning.

questions.question: Which status code means the request does not have valid authentication credentials?
questions.explanation: 401 Unauthorized indicates invalid authentication credentials.

questions.question: Which status code means the server understood the request but rejected it?
questions.explanation: 403 Forbidden means the request was understood but rejected.

questions.question: Which status code indicates that the requested resource path was not found on the server?
questions.explanation: 404 Not Found indicates the resource path was not found.

questions.question: What is the purpose of response pagination?
questions.explanation: Pagination breaks response data into chunks.

questions.question: Which six values are listed as accepted values for the Accept-Encoding request header? Select 6 answers.
questions.explanation: The module lists gzip, compress, deflate, br, identity, and *.

questions.question: Which three sequences are identified in the REST API request sequence diagram? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: The diagram is described as containing Create session, Get devices, and Create device sequences.

questions.question: Why do REST APIs generally require authentication?
questions.explanation: Authentication prevents random users from accessing or modifying information incorrectly or maliciously.
choices: To prevent unauthorized or malicious access and changes
To ensure every API is asynchronous
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent unauthorized or malicious access and changes

questions.question: What does authentication prove?
questions.explanation: Authentication proves the user's identity.

questions.question: What does authorization define?
questions.explanation: Authorization defines user access and permissions to perform an action on a resource.

questions.question: How does Basic authentication transmit credentials?
questions.explanation: It uses username/password pairs separated by a colon and encoded using Base64.
choices: Username/password pairs separated by a colon and Base64-encoded
A bearer token generated by an authentication server
An unencoded password without a username
questions.correctAnswer: Username/password pairs separated by a colon and Base64-encoded

questions.question: What does Bearer authentication use?
questions.explanation: Bearer authentication uses a bearer token generated by an authentication server such as an Identity Service.

questions.question: What is an API key as described in the module?
questions.explanation: It is a unique alphanumeric string generated by the server and assigned to a user.
choices: A unique alphanumeric string generated by the server and assigned to a user
A user's password encoded as XML
questions.correctAnswer: A unique alphanumeric string generated by the server and assigned to a user

questions.question: OAuth combines authentication with authorization.
questions.explanation: The module explicitly states this.

questions.question: What does OAuth 2.0 enable a third-party application to obtain?
questions.explanation: It enables limited access to an HTTP service.
choices: Limited access to an HTTP service
Unlimited server access without a token
questions.correctAnswer: Limited access to an HTTP service

questions.question: In OAuth, what is the process of obtaining an access token called?
questions.explanation: The process is called a flow.

questions.question: Which three purposes of API rate limiting are listed? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: Rate limiting helps avoid server overload, improve service/response time for users, and protect against DoS attacks.
choices: Avoid server overload from too many requests
Provide better service and response time to all users
correctAnswers: Avoid server overload from too many requests
Provide better service and response time to all users

questions.question: How does the leaky bucket algorithm process queued requests?
questions.explanation: Incoming requests can arrive at any rate, but the server processes the queue at a fixed rate.
choices: At the same rate at which every client sends them
Only after the queue becomes full

questions.question: What happens in the leaky bucket algorithm when the request queue is full?
questions.explanation: The request is rejected.
choices: The server doubles the queue automatically

questions.question: In the token bucket algorithm, what happens when a request is accepted?
questions.explanation: The server checks for a token, removes one, and processes the request.
choices: One token is removed and the request is processed
A new token is always added
The request is placed in a fixed-rate queue
questions.correctAnswer: One token is removed and the request is processed

questions.question: What happens when the token bucket contains no available token for a request?
questions.explanation: The server rejects the request.

questions.question: What does a fixed window counter assign to each fixed period of time?
questions.explanation: It assigns a counter representing how many requests can be processed during that period.
choices: A counter representing how many requests can be processed
questions.correctAnswer: A counter representing how many requests can be processed

questions.question: How does the sliding window counter decide whether to process a new request?
questions.explanation: It counts requests already made from the beginning of the window to the current time.
choices: It counts requests made from the beginning of the window to the current time
It checks only whether the previous request succeeded
It uses a queue processed at a fixed rate
It always accepts the first request from every client
questions.correctAnswer: It counts requests made from the beginning of the window to the current time

questions.question: What does the `X-Rate Limit-Limit` response header indicate?
questions.explanation: It indicates the maximum number of requests allowed in a specified unit of time.
choices: The maximum number of requests in a specified unit of time
The number of pending requests still available
The time when the window resets
questions.correctAnswer: The maximum number of requests in a specified unit of time

questions.question: What does the `X-Rate Limit-Remaining` header indicate?
questions.explanation: It gives the number of pending requests the requester can still make in the current window.
choices: The number of requests the requester can still make in the current window
The maximum requests allowed for all time
questions.correctAnswer: The number of requests the requester can still make in the current window

questions.question: What does the `X-Rate Limit-Reset` header indicate?
questions.explanation: It indicates when the rate-limit window will reset.
choices: When the rate-limit window will reset
questions.correctAnswer: When the rate-limit window will reset

questions.question: Which two HTTP status codes are identified as the most commonly used when a rate limit is exceeded? Select 2 answers.
questions.explanation: The module lists 429 Too Many Requests and 403 Forbidden.

questions.question: What is a webhook?
questions.explanation: A webhook is an HTTP callback, or HTTP POST to a specified URL, that notifies an application when a specified activity or event occurs.
choices: An HTTP callback or POST that notifies an application of an event
A polling loop that repeatedly requests all resources
A Git command for remote updates
questions.correctAnswer: An HTTP callback or POST that notifies an application of an event

questions.question: Why can webhooks make applications more efficient?
questions.explanation: They remove the need for polling mechanisms.

questions.question: Multiple applications can subscribe to a single webhook server.
questions.explanation: The module explicitly states this.

questions.question: Which three requirements must an application meet to consume webhook notifications? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: It must run continuously to receive POSTs, register a URI with the provider, and handle incoming notifications.
choices: Be running at all times to receive HTTP POST requests
Register a URI on the webhook provider
Handle incoming notifications from the webhook server
Create a Git branch for every event
correctAnswers: Be running at all times to receive HTTP POST requests
Register a URI on the webhook provider
Handle incoming notifications from the webhook server

questions.question: Which two resources should be kept handy when troubleshooting REST API issues? Select 2 answers.
questions.explanation: The module recommends the API reference guide and API authentication information.

questions.question: A REST API URI is missing its scheme. Which type of problem does the module use this to illustrate?
questions.explanation: A URI missing its scheme is the module's invalid URI example.

questions.question: Which four connectivity-related checks are raised when an API server cannot be reached? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation: The module asks about proxy, firewall, VPN, and SSL issues.

questions.question: The invalid-certificate issue described in the module can occur when the REST API URI uses HTTPS.
questions.explanation: The module states that this issue can occur with a secure HTTPS connection during SSL handshake.

questions.question: In the module's lab-environment example, which requests-library parameter can turn off certificate verification?
questions.explanation: The example adds `verify=False` to the request.

questions.question: What should be done when an API problem is caused by a server-side issue that cannot be resolved from the client side?
questions.explanation: The module says to contact the API server administrator.

questions.question: Which three troubleshooting steps are listed for interpreting HTTP errors? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: The module says to check the return code, check the response body, and use a status-code reference if needed.

questions.question: A request has malformed syntax because a resource is misspelled or a JSON object has a syntax issue. Which status code does the module associate with this situation?
questions.explanation: 400 Bad Request is associated with malformed syntax, including misspelled resources and JSON syntax issues.

questions.question: A server cannot authenticate a request because the credentials are invalid or missing. Which status code applies?
questions.explanation: 401 Unauthorized means the server could not authenticate the request.

questions.question: The server recognizes valid credentials, but the user lacks permission for the requested API. Which status code applies?
questions.explanation: 403 Forbidden means authentication is recognized but the client is not authorized.

questions.question: Which status code indicates that a client must authenticate itself with a proxy?
questions.explanation: 407 Proxy Authentication Required indicates proxy authentication is required.

questions.question: Multiple users are editing the same resource, producing a conflict with its current state. Which status code is associated with this example?
questions.explanation: The module uses an edit conflict as an example of 409.

questions.question: A client sends XML to a server that accepts only JSON. Which status code does the module associate with this problem?
questions.explanation: 415 Unsupported Media Type applies when the request body format is not supported.

questions.question: Which status code indicates that the server encountered an unexpected condition preventing it from fulfilling the request?
questions.explanation: 500 is Internal Server Error.

questions.question: Which status code indicates that the server does not support the functionality required to fulfill the request?
questions.explanation: 501 means Not Implemented.

questions.question: Which status code means a server acting as a gateway or proxy received an invalid response from an inbound server?
questions.explanation: 502 is Bad Gateway.

questions.question: Which status code means the server is currently unable to handle a request because of overload or scheduled maintenance?
questions.explanation: 503 is Service Unavailable.

questions.question: Which status code means a gateway or proxy did not receive a timely response from an upstream server?
questions.explanation: 504 is Gateway Timeout.
